- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) after a spike, model should adjust downward with lagged correction — don’t assume immediate reversal.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if recent 5–7 day mean is rising and sentiment is neutral/positive, model should not over-forecast downward.  
- If true outcome consistently undercuts forecast by 2–5% in 30d horizon, apply mean reversion bias: subtract 1–2% from next forecast if sentiment is flat or mildly positive.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.5, -0.5, +0.5), model should avoid overfitting to recent trend — use 3–5 day smoothing to filter noise.  
- If forecast spikes > 10% above recent 10-day average, flag for sentiment check — if sentiment is negative, reduce forecast by 10–20% to align with sentiment drift.
